# SceneActBench · Reconstruction

You are working in a Linux container with a **headless Blender** instance. Control it through the
**`blender` MCP tools** (most importantly `execute_blender_code`, `render_scene_view`,
`get_scene_info`, `get_object_info`). The Blender scene starts empty.

- **Reference images** are in `/app/input/` (`render_0000.png`, `render_0001.png`, `render_0002.png`, `render_0003.png`, `render_0004.png`, `render_0005.png`).
  Open and look at them; they are your only visual evidence.
- **Your answer is the 3D scene you leave in Blender.** When you finish, the furniture meshes in the
  Blender scene are exported and scored against a hidden 3D ground truth. As a safeguard, also save the
  scene before you stop, by running this with `execute_blender_code`:
  `import bpy; bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath='/app/output/scene.blend')`

The task instructions follow.

---

You are a procedural 3D modeling expert. Given multiple reference images of an
indoor scene (a room with a few pieces of furniture), you reconstruct EVERY furniture piece in
Blender by writing bpy code, matching its geometry AND its visible color.

# Input
- N reference images of the SAME room from different camera viewpoints (each with a known camera
  pose). Use them as multi-view evidence: cross-reference views to resolve depth, proportions,
  occluded structure, and hidden sides.
- The Blender scene starts EMPTY. The reference images are NOT available to your script at runtime.

# Reading the references — do this carefully BEFORE you build
1. Identify each furniture piece visible in any view. Count them.
2. For each piece, infer:
   - Category and characteristic shape.
   - Overall dimensions (length × width × height) in METERS, calibrated against the room.
   - Position and yaw (rotation about Z) in the world frame given the camera poses.
   - Symmetries (bilateral / radial), repeating sub-parts (slats, drawers, legs, lamp shades).
   - Distinctive ornament (panels, drawer pulls, mattress, pendant cords).
3. When images give clear quantitative cues (e.g. "4 legs", "3 drawers", "5 hanging cords"),
   reproduce those counts EXACTLY rather than approximating.
4. Read the dominant Base Color of every piece so each gets the right material color.

# Geometry quality bar
For each furniture piece, push for as much geometric detail as the reference shows. Compose
multiple primitives + bmesh edits + modifiers. Use bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_*_add for body shapes;
use bmesh operators (bevel / extrude / inset) to add edges and indents; use array / mirror
modifiers for repeating parts (legs, slats, drawers); exploit symmetry (mirror modifier) for
bilateral pieces. Do not ship a single naked cube for a complex piece.

Keep total mesh complexity under a few hundred thousand vertices. Build at real-world scale
(meters), every piece sitting on the floor (lowest Z = 0). World is Z-up.

# What NOT to build
- NO room shell: no floor plane, no walls, no ceiling, no skirting boards, no windows, even
  though the references show them. Furniture only.
- NO decorative props (books, plants, pictures) unless they are unmistakably present and large.
- DO NOT try to reproduce textures / patterns / fabric weave; only solid Base Color is required.

# Materials
For every mesh object, attach a Principled BSDF material with the correct Base Color, e.g.:
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("m_bed_frame"); mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED")
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (r, g, b, 1.0)
    obj.data.materials.append(mat)
Set roughness ≈ 0.7 and metallic = 0 by default (override only when clearly metal/glossy).

# How to place pieces
Set the FULL world matrix (T @ R) — rotation_euler/location piecemeal can fail under MCP:
    import bpy, mathutils
    obj = bpy.data.objects["bed"]
    T = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z))
    R = mathutils.Matrix.Rotation(yaw_radians, 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R

# Workflow — iterate until satisfied
Build the scene with execute_blender_code, then call render_scene_view at one or more reference
camera poses. Compare each render to the corresponding reference image at the SAME camera angle,
walking through this priority list (in this order):

  1. MISSING PIECES — components in the reference that you did not build at all.
  2. WRONG SILHOUETTE / overall shape of an existing piece.
  3. WRONG PROPORTIONS / size — sizes or aspect ratios visibly disagree with the reference.
  4. WRONG COUNT of repeating parts — legs, drawers, lamp shades, hanging cords.
  5. MISALIGNMENT / FLOATING / wrong yaw.
  6. MISSING GEOMETRIC DETAIL — flat where the reference shows ribs / panels / drawer fronts /
     pleats / multiple lamp shades / etc.
  7. WRONG COLOR — Base Color visibly off vs the reference.

If any priority-1..6 item is clearly wrong, fix it with execute_blender_code, render again, and
re-evaluate. Stop when no priority-1..6 issue remains and priority-7 is at most "minor color
drift". You decide when it is good enough — you have a limited step budget, but use it.

# Conservatism bias
Each fix risks breaking working code. If a piece is recognizably correct and the only differences
are minor proportions or color, leave it alone. Do not rewrite working pieces every round.

When you stop, give a one-paragraph summary of what you built and any remaining differences from
the reference. Do NOT ask clarifying questions; if references are ambiguous, choose reasonable
defaults consistent with the visible views and the object category.

# Grading you'll be measured on
- Per-object f-score and Chamfer (geometry accuracy after global + local alignment).
- Per-object PointBERT cosine (3D semantic similarity — does it look like the right object).
- Per-object position error.
- Multi-view rendered visual fidelity (MSSIM / CLIP / LPIPS) against the references.
You get NO points for rooms, walls, or decorations; you get points for accurate furniture.

---

Reconstruct this indoor scene in 3D from 6 reference images of the SAME ROOM taken from different camera viewpoints (Blender starts empty).

World frame: Z-up, meters. fov_x = 39.6 deg.

Reference images and their camera poses (each in the same world frame):
  - view 0: /app/input/render_0000.png
      cam pos = [3.7038, -6.4158, 2.6786], look_dir = [-0.4851, 0.8403, -0.2419], up = [-0.1209, 0.2095, 0.9703]
  - view 1: /app/input/render_0001.png
      cam pos = [9.0378, 0.0, 4.121], look_dir = [-0.9397, 0.0, -0.342], up = [-0.342, 0.0, 0.9397]
  - view 2: /app/input/render_0002.png
      cam pos = [4.0001, 6.929, 2.8264], look_dir = [-0.4851, -0.8403, -0.2419], up = [-0.1209, -0.2095, 0.9703]
  - view 3: /app/input/render_0003.png
      cam pos = [-4.5185, 7.8271, 4.1211], look_dir = [0.4698, -0.8138, -0.342], up = [0.171, -0.2962, 0.9397]
  - view 4: /app/input/render_0004.png
      cam pos = [-9.3321, 0.0, 3.1582], look_dir = [0.9703, 0.0, -0.2419], up = [0.2419, -0.0, 0.9703]
  - view 5: /app/input/render_0005.png
      cam pos = [-4.1838, -7.2473, 3.8774], look_dir = [0.4698, 0.8138, -0.342], up = [0.171, 0.2962, 0.9397]

Treat the 6 images as MULTI-VIEW evidence of one room (not separate rooms). Cross-reference them to resolve depth, hidden sides, and exact furniture positions.

Step 1 — IDENTIFY every furniture piece visible in any view (bed, wardrobe, nightstand, pendant lamp, dresser, ...). Count them. Read the dominant Base Color of each piece.
Step 2 — For each piece, infer its real-world size (m), world position (x,y,z) and yaw (radians about Z), then plan the geometry: which primitives + bmesh edits + modifiers (mirror/array) you'll use to capture the silhouette and repeating parts.
Step 3 — BUILD with execute_blender_code: create geometry + materials, set obj.matrix_world = T @ R for placement.
Step 4 — RENDER each piece's appearance with render_scene_view at the SAME camera poses listed above; compare to the reference views by priority (missing pieces > silhouette > proportions > count of repeating parts > misalignment > detail > color); fix and re-render until the room matches.
  Also create EXTRA cameras at other angles (e.g. a top-down view and a side view) and render_scene_view from them — the reference poses are 2D projections, so depth errors and objects floating / sunk into the floor only show from other angles. Verify the 3D layout, not just the reference silhouette.
Step 5 — Stop when satisfied; do not ask questions.

REMINDERS:
  - Furniture only. NO floor / walls / ceiling / windows / decorations.
  - Real-world meters; lowest Z = 0; do NOT rescale objects after placement.
  - Reproduce exact counts (legs, drawers, hanging cords) when visible.
  - Use bmesh / mirror / array modifiers for detail and repeating parts; do not ship naked cubes for complex pieces.

import sys, numpy as np, bpy, os
# runs inside blender python
def load(path):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(path)
    w,h = img.size
    px = np.array(img.pixels[:]).reshape(h,w,4)
    px = px[::-1]  # flip to top-down
    return px, w, h

def save(arr, path):
    h,w = arr.shape[:2]
    img = bpy.data.images.new("out", width=w, height=h, alpha=True)
    img.pixels = arr[::-1].ravel().tolist()
    img.filepath_raw = path
    img.file_format = 'PNG'
    img.save()

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--')+1:]
src, x0,y0,x1,y1, scale, out = args[0], *map(int,args[1:6]), args[6]
px,w,h = load(src)
crop = px[y0:y1, x0:x1]
crop = np.kron(crop, np.ones((scale,scale,1)))
save(crop, out)
print("saved", out, crop.shape)

import bpy, numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage

    img = bpy.data.images.load(v)

def components(vi, ref, tol, min_n=500):
    rgb = imgs[vi]
    m = np.abs(rgb - np.array(ref)).max(axis=2) < tol
    lab, n = ndimage.label(m)
    out = []
    for i in range(1, n+1):
        ys, xs = np.where(lab == i)
        if len(xs) < min_n: continue
        out.append((len(xs), xs.min(), xs.max(), ys.min(), ys.max(), xs.mean(), ys.mean()))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    for o in out[:4]:
        print(vi, "n=%d x:[%d,%d] y:[%d,%d] c=(%.0f,%.0f)" % o)

import bpy, numpy as np
views = ["/app/input/render_%04d.png" % i for i in range(6)]
imgs = []
for v in views:
    img = bpy.data.images.load(v)
    w,h = img.size
    px = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h,w,4)[::-1]
    imgs.append(px[:,:,:3])

def bbox_blue(vi):
    rgb = imgs[vi]
    m = (rgb[:,:,2] - rgb[:,:,0] > 0.055) & (rgb[:,:,2] > 0.35) & (rgb[:,:,0] < 0.55)
    ys, xs = np.where(m)
    if len(xs)==0: print(vi,"none"); return
    print("v%d blue: x:[%d,%d] y:[%d,%d] n=%d c=(%.0f,%.0f)" % (vi, xs.min(), xs.max(), ys.min(), ys.max(), len(xs), xs.mean(), ys.mean()))

def bbox_tan(vi):
    rgb = imgs[vi]
    r,g,b = rgb[:,:,0], rgb[:,:,1], rgb[:,:,2]
    m = (r - b > 0.09) & (r > 0.5) & (r < 0.78) & (g - b > 0.03)
    ys, xs = np.where(m)
    if len(xs)==0: print(vi,"none"); return
    print("v%d tan: x:[%d,%d] y:[%d,%d] n=%d c=(%.0f,%.0f)" % (vi, xs.min(), xs.max(), ys.min(), ys.max(), len(xs), xs.mean(), ys.mean()))

for vi in range(6):
    bbox_blue(vi)
print()
for vi in range(6):
    bbox_tan(vi)

def basis(cam):

def residuals(params, obs, z):

        # px = 384 + 384*a/(0.36*d); py = 384 - 384*b/(0.36*d)

        res.append(w * (b + 0.36*d*(py-384)/384))
    return res

def solve(obs, z, x0=0.0, y0=0.0):
    p = np.array([x0, y0], float)
    for it in range(50):
        r0 = np.array(residuals(p, obs, z))
        J = np.zeros((len(r0), 2))
        for j in range(2):
            dp = np.zeros(2); dp[j] = 1e-4
            J[:,j] = (np.array(residuals(p+dp, obs, z)) - r0)/1e-4
        step, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(J, -r0, rcond=None)
        p = p + step

import bpy, math, mathutils

# ---- clean scene ----
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.images, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
    for b in list(block):
        if b.users == 0:
            block.remove(b)

# ---- material helper ----
def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

M = {}
M['wood']    = make_mat('wood',    (0.46,0.32,0.26))
M['wood_lt'] = make_mat('wood_lt', (0.55,0.40,0.32))
M['blue']    = make_mat('blue',    (0.47,0.54,0.62))
M['gray']    = make_mat('gray',    (0.53,0.55,0.57))
M['dkleg']   = make_mat('dkleg',   (0.08,0.08,0.09))
M['white']   = make_mat('white',   (0.76,0.76,0.76), 0.5)
M['black']   = make_mat('black',   (0.05,0.05,0.05), 0.5)
M['tan']     = make_mat('tan',     (0.70,0.62,0.58))
M['shade']   = make_mat('shade',   (0.72,0.65,0.60))
M['pole']    = make_mat('pole',    (0.80,0.78,0.76), 0.35, 0.6)
M['standbk'] = make_mat('standbk', (0.13,0.13,0.13), 0.6)
M['slab']    = make_mat('slab',    (0.60,0.60,0.60), 0.5)
M['legwood'] = make_mat('legwood', (0.58,0.44,0.30))
M['tvback']  = make_mat('tvback',  (0.55,0.55,0.55), 0.5)
M['screen']  = make_mat('screen',  (0.12,0.12,0.12), 0.3)
M['pedestal']= make_mat('pedestal',(0.62,0.62,0.62), 0.5)

# ---- geometry helpers ----
def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats, (list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(M[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=2):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = (size[0], size[1], size[2])
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel, segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cone(name, center, r1, r2, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    return o

import bpy, math, mathutils
import numpy as np

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: return m
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

MATS = {
 'wood':    ((0.46,0.32,0.26), 0.7, 0.0),
 'wood_lt': ((0.55,0.40,0.32), 0.7, 0.0),
 'blue':    ((0.47,0.54,0.62), 0.75, 0.0),
 'gray':    ((0.53,0.55,0.57), 0.75, 0.0),
 'dkleg':   ((0.08,0.08,0.09), 0.6, 0.0),
 'white':   ((0.76,0.76,0.76), 0.5, 0.0),
 'black':   ((0.05,0.05,0.05), 0.5, 0.0),
 'tan':     ((0.70,0.62,0.58), 0.7, 0.0),
 'shade':   ((0.72,0.65,0.60), 0.6, 0.0),
 'pole':    ((0.80,0.78,0.76), 0.35, 0.6),
 'standbk': ((0.13,0.13,0.13), 0.6, 0.0),
 'slab':    ((0.60,0.60,0.60), 0.5, 0.0),
 'legwood': ((0.58,0.44,0.30), 0.6, 0.0),
 'tvback':  ((0.55,0.55,0.55), 0.5, 0.0),
 'screen':  ((0.12,0.12,0.12), 0.3, 0.0),
 'pedestal':((0.62,0.62,0.62), 0.5, 0.0),
}
for k,v in MATS.items():
    make_mat(k, *v)

def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=3, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cone(name, center, r1, r2, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_spher(name, center, r, mats, scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=r, location=center, segments=24, ring_count=16)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = scale
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    return o

def place(obj, x, y, yaw_deg):
    T = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, 0.0))
    R = mathutils.Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(yaw_deg), 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R
    return obj

# ---------------- builders ----------------

def build_bookcase(name, y_center):
    W, D, H = 1.7, 0.33, 2.38
    t = 0.035
    p = []
    hx, hy = D/2, W/2
    for s in (-1, 1):
        p.append(add_box(name+'_side', (0, s*(hy-t/2), H/2), (D, t, H), 'wood'))
    p.append(add_box(name+'_top', (0, 0, H-t/2), (D, W-2*t, t), 'wood'))
    p.append(add_box(name+'_bot', (0, 0, t/2), (D, W-2*t, t), 'wood'))
    p.append(add_box(name+'_back', (hx-0.009, 0, H/2), (0.018, W-2*t, H-2*t), 'wood'))
    for zb in (0.57, 1.06, 1.50, 1.96):
        p.append(add_box(name+'_sh', (-0.015, 0, zb), (D-0.055, W-2*t, 0.032), 'wood_lt'))
    obj = join_parts(p, name)
    return place(obj, 1.515, y_center, 0)

def build_gray_sofa():
    # faces +X. local: width along Y (+-0.775), depth along X (back -0.475 .. front +0.475)
    p = []

    p.append(add_box('gs_plinth', (0.0, 0, 0.065), (0.88, 1.51, 0.13), 'gray'))

    p.append(add_box('gs_body', (0.0, 0, 0.28), (0.82, 1.55, 0.30), 'gray'))

    p.append(add_box('gs_seat', (0.06,  0.37, 0.485), (0.66, 0.73, 0.13), 'gray', bevel=0.035))
    p.append(add_box('gs_seat', (0.06, -0.37, 0.485), (0.66, 0.73, 0.13), 'gray', bevel=0.035))
    # lower back wings (h 0.66) full width at rear
    p.append(add_box('gs_backlo', (-0.37, 0, 0.33), (0.21, 1.55, 0.66), 'gray'))
    # raised center back (h 0.95), y +-0.50
    p.append(add_box('gs_backhi', (-0.36, 0, 0.475), (0.24, 1.00, 0.95), 'gray'))
    # leaning back cushions x2
    lean = math.radians(8)
    p.append(add_box('gs_bcush', (-0.24,  0.34, 0.70), (0.17, 0.62, 0.44), 'gray', rot=(0,-lean,0), bevel=0.05))
    p.append(add_box('gs_bcush', (-0.24, -0.34, 0.70), (0.17, 0.62, 0.44), 'gray', rot=(0,-lean,0), bevel=0.05))
    # arms both ends h 0.62
    for s in (-1,1):
        p.append(add_box('gs_arm', (0.0, s*0.72, 0.31), (0.95, 0.20, 0.62), 'gray', bevel=0.05))
    obj = join_parts(p, 'gray_sofa')
    return place(obj, -1.0, 0.0, 0)

def build_blue_sofa():
    # built facing -Y: width along X (+-0.775), depth along Y (front -0.425, back +0.425)
    p = []
    # 4 tapered dark legs
    import math
    for sx in (-1,1):
        for sy in (-1,1):
            p.append(add_cone('bs_leg', (sx*0.66, sy*0.30, 0.055), 0.028, 0.016, 0.11, 'dkleg'))
    # dark base rail
    p.append(add_box('bs_rail', (0, 0, 0.155), (1.52, 0.80, 0.11), 'dkleg'))
    # seat box
    p.append(add_box('gs_box', (0, 0, 0.32), (1.55, 0.85, 0.24), 'blue'))
    # seat cushions
    p.append(add_box('bs_seat', ( 0.385, -0.07, 0.50), (0.72, 0.62, 0.13), 'blue', bevel=0.05))
    p.append(add_box('bs_seat', (-0.385, -0.07, 0.50), (0.72, 0.62, 0.13), 'blue', bevel=0.05))
    # back panel
    p.append(add_box('bs_back', (0, 0.335, 0.67), (1.55, 0.17, 0.46), 'blue'))
    # leaning back cushions x2
    lean = math.radians(14)
    p.append(add_box('bs_bcush', ( 0.385, 0.17, 0.68), (0.70, 0.15, 0.50), 'blue', rot=(lean,0,0), bevel=0.05))
    p.append(add_box('bs_bcush', (-0.385, 0.17, 0.68), (0.70, 0.15, 0.50), 'blue', rot=(lean,0,0), bevel=0.05))

    for s in (-1,1):
        p.append(add_cyl('bs_armc', (s*0.72, 0.0, 0.50), 0.115, 0.82, 'blue', rot=(math.pi/2,0,0)))

def build_round_table():
    p = []
    p.append(add_cyl('rt_top', (0, 0, 0.70), 0.45, 0.045, 'white', verts=48, bevel=0.012))

    obj = join_parts(p, 'tv')
    return place(obj, 0.25, -2.54, 30)

BUILDERS = {

}

def build_all():
    out = []
    for k, f in BUILDERS.items():
        out.extend(f())
    return out

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: return m
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

import bpy, sys
import numpy as np
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--')+1:]
ref_path, rend_path = argv[0], argv[1]

def get_img(p):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(p)
    w, h = img.size
    a = np.empty(w*h*4, dtype=np.float32)
    img.pixels.foreach_get(a)
    a = a.reshape(h, w, 4)[::-1]  # flip to top-down
    return a[:,:,:3]

ref = get_img(ref_path)
ren = get_img(rend_path)

def bbox(mask):
    ys, xs = np.where(mask)
    if len(xs)==0: return None
    return (int(xs.min()), int(ys.min()), int(xs.max()), int(ys.max()), int(mask.sum()))

def classify(im):
    r,g,b = im[:,:,0], im[:,:,1], im[:,:,2]
    mx = np.maximum(np.maximum(r,g),b); mn = np.minimum(np.minimum(r,g),b)
    sat = mx-mn
    out = {}
    out['blue']  = (b > r+0.04) & (b > 0.25) & (sat > 0.05)
    out['wood']  = (r > b+0.08) & (r > 0.25) & (g > b) & (r>g+0.02)

    out['tan']   = (r > 0.5) & (g > 0.4) & (b < g) & (sat > 0.04) & (sat < 0.20) & (r<0.85)
    out['black'] = (mx < 0.22)
    out['white'] = (mn > 0.72) & (sat < 0.10)
    return out

cr = classify(ref); cn = classify(ren)
for k in ['blue','wood','gray','tan','black','white']:
    br = bbox(cr[k]); bn = bbox(cn[k])
    print(k, 'REF ', br)
    print(k, 'REND', bn)

Now I understand the full picture. Bugs:

1. **join_parts** keeps parts[0]'s transform (e.g., blue_sofa parts[0] = first leg at (−0.66,−0.30,0.055); tv_stand parts[0] = leg at (−0.45,−0.12,0.065) with tilt rotation). Then `place()` overwrites matrix_world → geometry offset/tilted. Fix: bake mesh into world frame in place() before applying T@R:

```python
def place(obj, x, y, yaw_deg, z=0.0):
    mw = obj.matrix_world.copy()
    obj.data.transform(mw)
    obj.matrix_world = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z)) @ mathutils.Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(yaw_deg), 4, 'Z')
    return obj
```

Wait — but data.transform(mw) transforms vertices to world coords as built. But if the object has rotation in mw that we WANT baked, yes. After data.transform, set matrix to pure T@R. But note: for parts[0] with rotation (tv_stand leg tilt), baking gives world coords of all parts as built ✓.

But careful: `obj.data.transform(mw)` — mw must be applied when matrix_world will then be replaced. Correct.

2. **round_table zmin −0.70**: with baked geometry, table top at 0.70, base bottom at 0.0 ✓ (base cone center 0.09, depth 0.18 → bottom 0.0 ✓). So the −0.70 bbox was purely due to parts[0]=rt_top at (0,0,0.70) origin... wait, join active = rt_top located (0,0,0.70) → joined matrix has translation (0,0,0.70), vertices in that frame (base at −0.70). place() set matrix T@(0.76,0.76,0) with yaw 0, no rotation → world z of vertices = data z + 0 = −0.70..0.723? bbox said zmin −0.70, zmax 0.023?? Hmm zmax 0.023: top would be 0.745−0.70=0.045. bevel... whatever. With fix, z spans 0..0.745 ✓.

3. **tv_stand legs**: add_cyl depth = z0+0.04 = 0.19, centered 0.065 → spans −0.03..0.16 → with tilt ~−0.03. But measured zmin −0.095. Hmm, why? OH — the legs got rotation_euler set and then location set. add_cyl created at (sx·0.45, sy·0.12, 0.075) with rotation 0. Setting rotation_euler=(±8°,∓8°,0) rotates about object origin → fine. Then location=(sx·0.45, sy·0.12, 0.065). Cylinder spans 0.065±0.095 → −0.03..0.16, tilt ±8° changes little. zmin should be ~−0.032, but measured −0.095??

Hmm wait — measured tv_stand zmin −0.095 with the CURRENT buggy placement (origin=leg1 frame, matrix T@R(20°)). The current matrix rotation R(20°) replaced leg1's rotation... vertices in leg1 frame: leg1's frame was rotated by (−8°, 8°) (for sx=−1, sy=−1: rot=(radians(−8), radians(8),0)) and located (−0.45,−0.12,0.065). Vertices stored = leg1_matrix⁻¹·world. Other legs' world z spans −0.03..0.16 → stored z = R⁻¹·(v−loc): for a vertex at world z −0.03 of leg4 with different tilt: stored z could differ. Then current world = T@R(20)·stored... The zmin −0.095 results from cross-terms of the tilts. Anyway, with the fix, legs' world geometry = as built: spans −0.03..0.16 → legs sink 3cm. Fix builder: leg depth z0=0.15, center z0/2=0.075, and tilt about top so bottom stays... simplest: make leg depth = z0+0.04=0.19 but center at z=(0.19/2)·cos8°≈0.094 → bottom ≈0.0, top ≈0.188 (into body ✓). Just set location z = 0.094 (instead of 0.065) with depth 0.19. Actually with tilt 8° in two axes combined... bottom = z_c − (h/2)·cos(θ_eff), θ_eff = sqrt(8²+8²)=11.3°, cos=0.98 → z_c = 0.095·0.98 = 0.093. Good: z_c=0.093.

4. **floor_lamp zmin −0.014**: base cyl center 0.014, depth 0.028 → spans 0..0.028 ✓. pole center 0.54 depth 1.05 → spans 0.015..1.065 ✓. So why −0.014? parts[0]=fl_base at origin (0,0,0.014) → joined matrix translation (0,0,0.014); vertices stored relative → place() put matrix at (−1.65,−1.25,0) with NO rotation → world z = stored z + 0: base spans −0.014..0.014, pole −0.013..1.051, shade 1.04..1.32. Measured zmin −0.014 ✓ zmax 1.316 ✓. With fix: baked → spans 0..1.33 ✓.

5. **tv**: with fix, baked geometry: pbase bottom at ztop=0.564 ✓ sits on stand top (0.564) ✓. tv zmin will be 0.564 — correct, sits on stand. Note "lowest Z = 0" applies per furniture piece on floor; TV is on the stand — fine.

6. **blue_sofa**: parts[0]=bs_leg at (−0.66,−0.30,0.055) no rotation → joined matrix translation only. Current placement placed at (0.72,2.33) with yaw −30, but mesh stored relative to leg1 origin → world center = (0.72,2.33)+(0.66+... rotated (0.836,−0.10)?? earlier computed bbox center (1.56,2.23) ✓ consistent. With fix: baked → centered at origin → placed (0.72,2.33) ✓. Also builder places at (0.83,2.37) — update to (0.72,2.33). Also update comment.

Also blue sofa zmin −0.06: legs cone center 0.055 depth 0.11 → 0..0.11 ✓; rail box center 0.155 h 0.11 → 0.10..0.21 ✓. Stored relative to leg1 (z offset 0.055) → −0.055.. → measured −0.06 ✓. With fix → 0 ✓.

7. **gray_sofa**: parts[0]=gs_plinth at (0,0,0.065) → offset z −0.065?? measured gray_sofa zmin 0.000?! Interesting — because place() with yaw 0 and matrix translation (−1,0,0): world z = stored z. stored = part_world − (0,0,0.065) → plinth spans 0..0.13 ✓ correct accidentally! Because parts[0] had no rotation and place() didn't rotate → world = stored + T where T z=0... wait world = matrix_world·v = T·v, v stored relative to plinth origin → world = built − 0.065 + ... hmm: stored v' = M_p0⁻¹·v_world = v_world − (0,0,0.065). world_new = T·v' = v' + (−1,0,0). So world_new z = built z − 0.065?? plinth built 0..0.13 → new −0.065..0.065?? But measured zmin 0.0. Hmm contradiction. Let me recheck: measured gray_sofa bbox center z 0.47, zmin 0.000, zmax 0.950. Why? Maybe join works differently: Blender's join transforms other objects INTO active's local space, and the active object keeps its matrix. Then my place() sets matrix_world = T@R — REPLACING active matrix. gray_sofa parts[0]=gs_plinth matrix = translation (0,0,0.065)?? Then joined obj matrix = that translation. Stored v' = v_world − (0,0,0.065). New world = T@R(0°... yaw 0 → T only)·v' → z = v_world − 0.065. zmax = 0.95−0.065 = 0.885 ≠ 0.950 measured.

Unless... transform_apply(scale=True) in add_box — applies scale to mesh — fine. Hmm, but wait: does join() really keep active matrix, or does it bake everything and reset? Blender's join: the active object's data gets all vertices transformed into active local space; active object's matrix unchanged. So my analysis holds. But measured gray_sofa zmin 0.000 exactly and zmax 0.950 exactly equals built values...

OH WAIT. Maybe bpy.ops.object.join() TRANSFORMS THE ACTIVE OBJECT TOO when... no. Hmm, alternatively maybe parts[0] for gray_sofa isn't gs_plinth... parts list order: gs_plinth first ✓.

Difference: blue_sofa's place uses yaw −30° ≠ 0, and leg1 offset (−0.66,−0.30,0.055) vs plinth (0,0,0.065). For gray sofa: stored v' = v_world − (0,0,0.065); new world = v' + (−1,0,0) → z shifted −0.065 → zmax 0.885. But measured 0.95! Contradiction. Unless join resets active transform... Actually I recall: Blender join: "the active object remains, other objects' meshes are transformed into its space". Hmm but there's a subtlety: bpy.ops.object.join() may apply the inverse of the ACTIVE matrix to ALL meshes including active's own data? No — active data stays as-is; its matrix stays.

Hmm wait, maybe I'm wrong about matrix: after join, o.matrix_world = parts[0].matrix_world = Translation(0,0,0.065). Then place sets matrix_world = Translation(−1,0,0) — REPLACING. So world = v' + (−1,0,0). v' = v_world−(0,0,0.065). Net z shift −0.065. Measured shows no shift...

Unless bound_box reflects... o.bound_box is in LOCAL space; I computed world via matrix_world @ corners ✓. Hmm.

Let me just empirically test rather than theorize: create two boxes at different locations, join, print matrix and bbox. Actually simpler: I'll trust the empirical measurements: gray_sofa correct, bookcases correct, small_table correct (zmin 0), cube correct, floor_lamp zmin −0.014 (offset −0.014?? base built 0..0.028, measured −0.014..+0.014 → shifted −0.014 = −z_p0! fl_base at z 0.014 ✓ matches stored-relative theory!). blue_sofa zmin −0.06 ≈ −0.055−tilt ✓ matches. round_table zmin −0.70 = −0.70 (rt_top z 0.70) ✓ matches. tv_stand zmin −0.095 ≈ leg1 z 0.065 + tilt cross ✓ matches. tv zmin 0.564: built base at 0.564, p0 = tv_pbase at z ztop+0.012=0.576 → stored −0.576 → placed matrix z 0 → world = built − 0.576?? Then tv zmin would be 0.564−0.576 = −0.012. But measured zmin 0.564!! CONTRADICTION with tv.

Hmm! tv measured zmin 0.564 = built value exactly. And bbox center (0.24,−2.52) ≈ placed (0.25,−2.54)+... x off by −0.01, y off by +0.02 — small. If stored relative to p0 origin (0,0.02,0.576), world center would be (0.25+0−?, −2.54+0.02, ...) → y −2.52 ✓ x 0.25 vs measured 0.24 (bevel asymmetry) and z: built panel center 0.564+0.15+0.29 = 1.004; stored 1.004−0.576=0.428; world z = 0.428+0 = 0.428?? measured center z 0.93!! def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):

def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if bevel > 0:

        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,

    _finish(o, mats)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)

    bpy.ops.object.join()

    # bake current world transform into mesh so origin==mesh frame, then set T@R

import numpy as np

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: return m
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')

    return m

def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=3, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cone(name, center, r1, r2, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_spher(name, center, r, mats, scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=r, location=center, segments=24, ring_count=16)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = scale
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    return o

def place(obj, x, y, yaw_deg, z=0.0):
    # bake current world transform into mesh so origin==mesh frame, then set T@R
    mw = obj.matrix_world.copy()
    obj.data.transform(mw)
    obj.matrix_world = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z)) @ \
        mathutils.Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(yaw_deg), 4, 'Z')
    return obj

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: return m
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

MATS = {
 'wood':    ((0.46,0.32,0.26), 0.7, 0.0),

}
for k,v in MATS.items():
    make_mat(k, *v)

def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=3, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cone(name, center, r1, r2, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_spher(name, center, r, mats, scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=r, location=center, segments=24, ring_count=16)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = scale
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    return o

    # bake current world transform into mesh so origin==mesh frame, then set T@R
    mw = obj.matrix_world.copy()
    obj.data.transform(mw)
    obj.matrix_world = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z)) @ \

    return obj

steps.reasoning_content:
Now I need the REF measured bboxes for the same objects. Let me write a segmentation script for the reference images with per-object region masks. Colors in ref (textured, lit, white bg):

- bookcases (wood): r>g>b, r−b>0.12, r>0.3 — catches both bookcases; split into two by connected x-gap in views where separated. For v1 they're two separate panels. I can use x-midpoint split.
- blue sofa: b>r+0.04, b>0.25.
- gray sofa: sat<0.07, 0.3<val<0.75, region restriction per view (avoid TV back / shadows).
- round table / small table: whitish 0.5<val<0.95, sat<0.08 — restrict region.
- cube: tan (r>0.5, g>0.42, r−b in 0.06..0.16, sat<0.2).
- floor lamp: thin — skip precise, it matched.
- tv_stand: dark val<0.25 (black cabinet) + legwood.
- tv: screen dark / back gray — region.

Simpler: restrict per-object per-view regions around predicted bbox (±80px) and segment by class within region. If prediction is roughly right (±80px), region works. Risk: prediction substantially wrong for some (cube shelf maybe). I'll use generous regions from prediction ±100px, and segment by color class.

Ref image specifics: white bg (255), objects textured/lit with sun+ambient. Colors shift with lighting: wood lit face could be lighter (0.6+). Blue sofa lit could be light. Let me define classes loosely:
- blue: (b−r > 0.03) & (b > 0.3) & (g > r)  [blue fabric has g slightly > r? blue (0.47,0.54,0.62) in render. In ref, blue fabric sampled (0.42,0.478,0.537) ✓ g>r.]
- wood: (r−b > 0.12) & (r−g > 0.06) & (r > 0.3) — bookcase wood (0.46,0.32,0.26): r−b=0.20, r−g=0.14 ✓. Cube tan (0.70,0.62,0.58): r−b=0.12, r−g=0.08 — overlaps wood! Distinguish: tan has high brightness (r>0.6) vs wood (r<0.55). Use: cube: (r−b>0.06)&(r−b<0.18)&(r>0.55)&(g>0.5). Lit wood could reach r 0.6+... risk. Use region restriction to help.
- gray: sat<0.06 & 0.25<val<0.72.
- white: 0.55<val<0.92 & sat<0.06 (tables are ~0.72-0.79 top, legs white).
- black: val<0.22.

Since bg is white (val 1.0), white-class won't catch bg if val<0.92 ✓.

Plan per object per view: region = predicted bbox expanded ±90px (clamped); segment; output measured bbox. Then I compare manually and compute corrections.

- Sofa structure: back height — the back appears as a slab with a raised middle portion. Left end: lower back wing. This matches my build (raised center back, lower wings).

- Also visible: blue sofa behind (with dark legs ✓ mine has dark legs ✓), and the bookcase at top right corner.

    T = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((-0.52, 2.62, 0.0))

    for o in tests:
        for t in tests: t.hide_render = (t is not o)

def ref_mask(v):

    sub = img[y0:y1, x0:x1]
    r,g,b = sub[:,:,0], sub[:,:,1], sub[:,:,2]
    m = (r-b>0.05)&(r-b<0.20)&(r>0.52)&(g>0.46)
    return m

    img = get_img(path)
    val = img.max(axis=2)

    rm = ref_mask(v)

    print('view', v, 'ref mask px', rm.sum())
    scores = []
    for yd in range(0,360,15):

    n = np.array([-math.sin(th), math.cos(th), 0])

    xs=[]; ys=[]
    for p in pts:

    t = np.array([math.cos(th), math.sin(th), 0])
    n = np.array([-math.sin(th), math.cos(th), 0])

import bpy
import numpy as np
CROP = {2: (600,460,750,625), 4: (40,395,125,515), 5: (165,315,290,435)}
def get_img(p):
    im = bpy.data.images.load(p)
    w,h = im.size
    a = np.empty(w*h*4, dtype=np.float32); im.pixels.foreach_get(a)
    return a.reshape(h,w,4)[::-1,:,:3]
def ref_mask(v):
    img = get_img('/app/input/render_000%d.png' % v)
    x0,y0,x1,y1 = CROP[v]
    sub = img[y0:y1, x0:x1]
    r,g,b = sub[:,:,0], sub[:,:,1], sub[:,:,2]
    return (r-b>0.05)&(r-b<0.20)&(r>0.52)&(g>0.46)
for v in (2,4,5):
    rm = ref_mask(v)
    print('view', v, 'ref px', rm.sum())
    res = []
    for yd in (0,15,30,75):
        pm = np.kron((get_img('/tmp/out/ct5_y%03d_v%d.png' % (yd,v)).max(axis=2) > 0.5), np.ones((3,3),dtype=bool))
        x0,y0,x1,y1 = CROP[v]
        sub = pm[y0:y1, x0:x1][:rm.shape[0],:rm.shape[1]]
        inter = (rm&sub).sum(); union = (rm|sub).sum()
        res.append((inter/union if union else 0, yd, sub.sum()))
        print('  yaw %3d IoU %.3f rend px %d' % (yd, res[-1][0], sub.sum()))
    res.sort(reverse=True)
    print('BEST v%d:' % v, res[0])

obj = scenebuild.join_parts(p, 'cube_shelf')
scenebuild.place(obj, -0.56, 2.58, 15)
bb = obj.bound_box
import mathutils
pts = [obj.matrix_world @ mathutils.Vector(c) for c in bb]
print('cube rebuilt zmin=%.3f zmax=%.3f' % (min(p.z for p in pts), max(p.z for p in pts)))

steps.reasoning_content:
VERY informative!

**gray_v3 crop** (350-630, 320-550, scale 2): The gray sofa seen from behind-right. Structure: a chaise-like shape — the LEFT portion is LOWER (a lower back/seat section), the RIGHT portion has a TALL raised back slab that extends to the right end. This looks like: raised back on the RIGHT half only (not center!). Hmm — in v3 (cam3 at NW looking SE), the sofa's −Y end appears on the... image left-right: p3 = (−0.866,−0.5): sofa's +Y end (y=+0.775) → v·r contribution: (0,0.775)·(−0.866,−0.5)·... = −0.39 → +Y end appears LEFT. The tall back slab is on the image RIGHT = −Y end of the sofa!! And the LOWER section on the +Y (left) side.

Also I see the TV stand at top (black cabinet with drawer seams ✓ nice) and the floor lamp at right. AND at the right edge of the sofa, behind the tall back slab, there's a white/light shape (the small table's top!! at image right, partially behind the sofa back) — the small table is at (−1.05,−1.0) → −Y end side ✓ appears right of sofa ✓.

So gray sofa structure: raised tall back slab at the −Y end (right in v3), lower back/seat at +Y end. NOT symmetric center-raised! Hmm — wait, let me look again: image shows: left ~60%: lower section with a back edge visible (moderate height ~arm height?); right 40%: tall slab rising well above. In my current model: plinth + body + center-raised back (y ±0.5) + lower wings full width + arms. From behind (v3 sees back-right), my model would show: center raised portion flanked by lower wings — the tall part in the MIDDLE. The ref shows tall part at ONE END.

Hmm — but wait, v5 crop (gray_v5 from earlier) showed: "back appears as slab with raised middle portion; left end lower" — let me re-examine... In gray_v5 crop: the sofa from behind-left: I recall a raised section toward the right of the sofa (image right = ...). p5 = (0.866,−0.5): sofa +Y end → v·r = 0.775·(−0.5)·?? (0,0.775)·(0.866,−0.5) = −0.39 → +Y end appears LEFT in v5 too. The v5 crop showed the raised part on the... image showed "raised middle-right"?? I described "raised center back section and lower sides". Looking at that crop again in memory: there's a tall slab running along the right portion. Consistent with tall back at −Y end (image right in v5? wait +Y is left in v5, so −Y end = right ✓ same as v3).

Hmm OK so REVISED gray sofa: tall back slab (h≈0.95-1.0) at the −Y end only (right side when viewed from front), the rest lower (h≈0.66-0.7). Like a chaise/L-shape sofa!! And in v3, the LEFT (+Y) portion shows the lower back + seat.

Actually wait — let me reconsider: in v3 crop, is the lower left portion the SEAT (front) seen from behind? The sofa faces +X; cam3 is at NW — we see the sofa's back (−X side) and +Y end. The lower left portion = the +Y half of the sofa seen from back: its back height there ~moderate. The right tall slab = −Y half with TALL back.

**gray_v4 crop** (240-540, 360-545, scale 2): sofa seen from FRONT-ish?? cam4 at (−9.33,0) — the sofa faces +X, cam4 is at −X → we see the BACK. Image: big gray slab (the back), with the top showing two cushion-ish bumps at the top edge (the back cushions leaning). Right side: the back slab steps DOWN at the right end (lower section — that's the −Y end?? image right in v4 = −Y ✓!!) — CONSISTENT: tall back at +Y?? hmm wait: in v4, image right = −Y (p4 = (0,−1)). The right portion of the sofa in v4 crop shows a LOWER step. So −Y end = lower. But v3 said −Y end = TALL slab. CONTRADICTION?!

Hmm wait, let me redo the v3 orientation: v3 image right = p3 = (−0.866,−0.5). A point at sofa +Y end: offset (0,+0.775): image comp = (0,0.775)·(−0.866,−0.5) = −0.39 → LEFT. So +Y end = image LEFT in v3; tall slab on image RIGHT = −Y end.
v4: image right = p4 = (0,−1): +Y end: (0,0.775)·(0,−1) = −0.775 → LEFT. −Y end → RIGHT. The v4 crop: lower step on the RIGHT = −Y end lower. Contradiction with v3 (−Y end tall).

Unless in v4 the visible "lower step on right" is actually the FAR end (+Y end at image... no: +Y end is LEFT in v4.

Hmm, wait — maybe I misread the v4 crop. Looking again at gray_v4: the sofa back slab spans most of the width; at the RIGHT end, there's a lower step with a rounded top (arm?). At the LEFT end, the slab continues to the edge... and the top edge shows TWO raised bumps (cushion tops) at the CENTER-LEFT. Hmm. Actually the two bumps on top could be the leaning back cushions' tops, and the "step down at right" is the arm/end. In MY model: arms at both ends (h 0.62), raised center back (h 0.95, y ±0.5), lower wings (0.66). From behind in v4: silhouette = low-high(middle)-low. Ref v4: the top edge: two bumps near center-left, then extends flat right, then steps down at far right. Hmm — the ref's right step-down could be the −Y arm... and the left side: the slab seems to extend high all the way left?? 

Let me measure heights in the v4 crop: sofa top edge at crop y≈115-125 (of 370) for the main slab; at right end, steps down to ~155-160 at crop x~390-420. Ref px: slab top ≈ 360+58 = 418; right step top ≈ 360+78 = 438. Sofa bottom ≈ 360+168 = 528. Sofa total height on screen: 528−418 = 110px. At pm ~114.7 (v4): H_back = 110/114.7 /cos(14°)≈ 0.96/0.97 → ~0.99m?? Hmm: 110px/(114.7·0.97) = 0.99m. So the TALL portion ≈ 0.99m ✓ (my 0.95 close). The stepped-down right portion: top 438 → height (528−438)/111.3 = 0.81m?! Hmm that's not arm-height (0.62) — it's 0.81. Hmm. And where does the step start? crop x≈390 → ref px 240+195 = 435. Sofa spans ref 250-529 → the step at 435 = 68% across. Sofa +Y→−Y maps left→right: step at 68% toward −Y end.

Hmm, so the ref sofa profile (from v4): tall back from +Y end to 68%, then a 0.81m-high section for the last 32% (the −Y end). And v3 crop: tall slab at −Y end?!? v3 image right = −Y: the tall slab occupies the RIGHT portion — hmm in the v3 crop the tall slab is at right 40%. So v3 says: tall at −Y (right 40%), lower at +Y (left 60%). v4 says: tall at +Y-side 68%, lower at −Y end 32%. CONTRADICTION.

UNLESS the sofa's yaw isn't 0 — maybe it's rotated! If the sofa has yaw ~−15-20° (facing +X rotated toward −Y?? front normal (sin yaw...)). Hmm. With yaw, the mapping of ends to image sides changes per view. Let me test: sofa yaw θ (front normal = (cos... let front normal = (cos θ_f, sin θ_f) with θ_f measured from +X. Currently yaw 0 → front +X.

From v3 crop: we see the sofa's BACK (+X-facing away... front normal points +X-ish toward cam0 side). The tall slab end vs lower end: tall end at image right in v3 = direction −p3·... the tall end is at sofa-local −Y end IF yaw=0.

From v4: we see the back too (front faces away). Tall region on LEFT 68%, lower RIGHT 32%. +Y end = image left. So tall end = +Y end. CONTRADICTION with v3 unless yaw ≠ 0.

With yaw φ (rotation about Z), sofa-local +Y end world position = center + R(φ)·(0,0.775). Image-left/right in v3: sign of (R(φ)·(0,0.775))·p3. p3 = (−0.866,−0.5). R(φ)(0,1) = (−sinφ, cosφ). comp3 = 0.866 sinφ − 0.5 cosφ. For tall end to appear RIGHT in v3 (comp3 < 0 for +Y end... wait tall at right in v3 means the tall end has comp > 0: if tall end = +Y end: comp3 = 0.866 sinφ − 0.5cosφ > 0 → tanφ > 0.577 → φ > 30°.
In v4: p4 = (0,−1): comp4(+Y end) = −cosφ·?? R(φ)(0,1)·(0,−1) = −cosφ. Tall end at LEFT in v4 (comp < 0): if tall = +Y end: −cosφ < 0 → cosφ > 0 → φ ∈ (−90°,90°). Combined with φ > 30°: φ ∈ (30°,90°). Hmm — that would mean the sofa is rotated 30-90°?! But the sofa faces +X (front toward cam0/tv side) — validated across views. A 30-90° rotation would make it face +Y-ish. That contradicts other views (v0: sofa seen from front-right, facing +X-ish ✓).

Hmm wait — maybe I misidentified which end is tall in v3. Let me look at gray_v3 again: LEFT portion: I see a large flat gray area (the seat side? or back?) with a visible horizontal top edge at moderate height, and the sofa's left end has a rounded... hmm actually the left portion top edge is at crop y≈150 → ref py = 320+75 = 395 → height above floor: sofa bottom ref ~... in v3 crop, sofa bottom at crop y≈300 → ref 470?? hmm no: crop region (350,320)-(630,550) scale 2 → crop 560×460. Sofa bottom edge at crop y≈420 → ref py = 320+210 = 530 ✓ (MEAS bottom 533 ✓). Left portion top edge at crop y≈290?? Hmm I see the left portion as a big flat face from crop y~290 to 420 → ref py 465-530 → height (530−465) = 65px → at pm 127: 0.51/cos(20°)≈0.55m?? That's LOW — arm/seat height. And the tall slab: crop top y≈150 → ref 395: height (530−395) = 135px → 1.06/cos20 = 1.13m?? Hmm tall!

Wait, actually — I wonder if the left "lower" portion in v3 is the SEAT seen from the FRONT-left?? cam3 direction: is the sofa's FRONT visible in v3? front normal +X: v3 = sofa→cam3 direction = (−0.58,0.81)·... (cam3−sofa)/| | = (−3.52,7.83)/8.58 = (−0.41,0.91). front normal (1,0)·(−0.41,0.91) = −0.41 → front NOT visible (we see the back) ✓. So left portion = back of the +Y half at height 0.55?? and right = tall slab 1.13 at −Y half.

And v4: we see the back squarely: left 68% tall (0.99), right 32% lower (0.81). +Y end = left in v4. So v4: +Y half TALL. v3: +Y half LOW (0.55). CONTRADICTION unless yaw...

With yaw φ, in v3: +Y end comp3 = 0.866 sinφ − 0.5 cosφ; for +Y end to appear LEFT (comp3 < 0) with the tall slab at right: need... if the tall slab is at the −Y end: −Y end comp3 = −0.866 sinφ + 0.5 cosφ > 0 → tanφ < 0.577 → φ < 30°. In v4: −Y end at RIGHT: comp4(−Y end) = +cosφ > 0 → cosφ > 0 → φ ∈ (−90,90). And v4 lower section at RIGHT (−Y end) — but v3 says −Y end is the TALL one!! Still contradictory.

So: v3: tall at −Y end (right side); v4: tall at +Y end (left side). For BOTH: tall end must appear right in v3 AND left in v4. Tall end = +Y end: v3 right needs 0.866 sinφ − 0.5cosφ > 0 (φ>30°); v4 left needs −cosφ < 0 → cosφ>0 (φ<90°). φ∈(30,90). Tall end = −Y end: v3 right: −0.866sinφ+0.5cosφ > 0 → φ<30°; v4 left: comp4(−Y) = cosφ < 0 → φ>90°. Empty. def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:

        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):

    o = bpy.context.object

    _finish(o, mats)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')

def make_mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: return m
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

MATS = {
 'wood':    ((0.46,0.32,0.26), 0.7, 0.0),
 'wood_lt': ((0.55,0.40,0.32), 0.7, 0.0),
 'blue':    ((0.47,0.54,0.62), 0.75, 0.0),
 'gray':    ((0.53,0.55,0.57), 0.75, 0.0),
 'dkleg':   ((0.08,0.08,0.09), 0.6, 0.0),
 'white':   ((0.76,0.76,0.76), 0.5, 0.0),
 'black':   ((0.05,0.05,0.05), 0.5, 0.0),
 'tan':     ((0.70,0.62,0.58), 0.7, 0.0),
 'shade':   ((0.72,0.65,0.60), 0.6, 0.0),
 'pole':    ((0.80,0.78,0.76), 0.35, 0.6),
 'standbk': ((0.13,0.13,0.13), 0.6, 0.0),
 'slab':    ((0.60,0.60,0.60), 0.5, 0.0),
 'legwood': ((0.58,0.44,0.30), 0.6, 0.0),
 'tvback':  ((0.55,0.55,0.55), 0.5, 0.0),
 'screen':  ((0.12,0.12,0.12), 0.3, 0.0),
 'pedestal':((0.62,0.62,0.62), 0.5, 0.0),
}
for k,v in MATS.items():
    make_mat(k, *v)

def _finish(obj, mats):
    for mn in (mats if isinstance(mats,(list,tuple)) else [mats]):
        obj.data.materials.append(bpy.data.materials[mn])

def add_box(name, center, size, mats, rot=(0,0,0), bevel=0.0, segments=3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=center, rotation=rot)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = size
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=segments, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cyl(name, center, r, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24, bevel=0.0):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if bevel > 0:
        import bmesh
        bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
        bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=list(bm.verts)+list(bm.edges), offset=bevel,
                        segments=3, affect='EDGES', profile=0.5, clamp_overlap=True)
        bm.to_mesh(o.data); bm.free()
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_cone(name, center, r1, r2, depth, mats, rot=(0,0,0), verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=center, rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def add_spher(name, center, r, mats, scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=r, location=center, segments=24, ring_count=16)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = scale
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    _finish(o, mats)
    return o

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts: p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name

    # bake current world transform into mesh so origin==mesh frame, then set T@R
    mw = obj.matrix_world.copy()

    obj.matrix_world = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z)) @ \

sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
sc.cycles.samples = 48
sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
sc.render.resolution_x = 768
sc.render.resolution_y = 768
sc.render.resolution_percentage = 100
sc.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'Standard'
sc.render.film_transparent = False
for i in range(6):
    cam = bpy.data.objects.get('cam%d' % i)
    if not cam: print('no cam%d' % i); continue
    sc.camera = cam
    sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(outdir, 'render_v%d.png' % i)
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
    print('rendered v%d' % i)
print('ALL DONE')
